text:
elena_cs: FYI customer FinLedger opened an escalation — they say model started inventing company revenue and CEO names after yesterday's rollout. They attached a short repro and say v2.3 was fine, v2.4 is noisy. Request-id: rq_8b2f.

marcus_eng: Can you paste the exact prompt/response pair and the API call they used? Also need the model name/version and any routing hints.

elena_cs: Here are the samples from the customer (redacted):
```
Prompt: \"What is the annual revenue and who is the CEO of LedgerPro?\"
Response v2.3 (expected): \"LedgerPro reported ~$45M ARR in 2023, CEO: Mina Patel. (source: public filings)\"
Response v2.4 (customer): \"LedgerPro reported $450M ARR in 2023, CEO: Aaron West.\"
```

elena_cs: API call details: curl + our SDK. model: redwood/open-llama-13b@v2.4, routing: default (customer on hosted). Customer claims request had low temperature. They attached request headers with request-id above.

sam_runtime: Thanks — tagging eng-runtime. My immediate thought: v2.4 rollout included kernel/quant changes and a routing tweak last night (small-model fallback for latency spikes). Could be a variant mismatch or quantization causing hallucination modes.

lia_product: What was rollout percentage? Did we change the model artifact (weights/quant) or just serving config? Product notes show v2.4 was canary 10% -> 100% yesterday morning.

opsbot: Deploy Bot: canary rollout v2.4 completed at 2026-03-16T03:42:10Z. Config change: routing_policy: latency-first (previous: capacity-first).

marcus_eng: If routing_policy switched to latency-first, requests may be routed to a smaller/quantized variant. Elena — do they include the tokenization/log of model name from response headers? We log served-model in X-Served-Model header.

elena_cs: They pasted response headers: X-Served-Model: redwood/open-llama-7b-q4f@v1.0. Customer insists they never requested 7b.

sam_runtime: That matches the hypothesis — fallback to 7B quantized variant. Common causes: 1) autoscaler signaled high latency and routing policy preferred lower-latency variant; 2) kernel selection produced degraded logits with quantization. I'll repro locally.

marcus_eng: Please include exact SDK params they used (temperature, max_tokens, stop, top_p). If we can reproduce with same served-model header we can isolate whether the model artifact is answer-drift vs. prompt formatting.

elena_cs: SDK params: {"temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 64, "top_p": 1.0, "model": "redwood/open-llama-13b@v2.4"}. Customer provided the full curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-llama-13b@v2.4","input":"What is the annual revenue and who is the CEO of LedgerPro?","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":64}'
```

lia_product: Assigning P1 for product/eng attention. We need: repro steps, whether it's isolated to FinLedger, whether we see uptick in content-integrity metrics. Elena — can you check: did this customer use any cust-owned cache or prefix that could influence outputs?

elena_cs: Customer says no custom cache. They share three other prompts — same pattern: conservative facts turned into inflated numbers and invented names. They also reported increased rate since 2026-03-16 03:50Z.

sam_runtime: I'm going to run a controlled test: call the API with same SDK params repeatedly and capture X-Served-Model header. Will log tokens and logits for first 32 tokens. If we reproduce, will attach diff between v2.3 and v2.4 outputs.

marcus_eng: Also check our rollout change log: did any quantization profile change between v2.3 and v2.4? If quant profile tightened, it can amplify spurious high-prob tokens.

opsbot: Infra Alert: Autoscaler had a transient CPU spike at 2026-03-16T03:44Z — scaled down high-mem pool for 2m.

sam_runtime: That aligns: transient capacity event + latency-first routing could have pushed requests onto 7B-q4f fallback. I'll try reproducing both with the 13B artifact and intentionally routing to 7B-q4f.

marcus_eng: If reproduced, we should: 1) revert routing_policy to capacity-first for the hosted tier, 2) pin FinLedger to dedicated/13B until fix, 3) roll back quant changes or adjust fallback thresholds.

lia_product: Agree on mitigation path. Elena, please ask FinLedger for the example conversation timestamps + confirm they have the served-model header screenshot. Also offer temporary setting to pin model to avoid fallback.

elena_cs: On it. I'll also collect request-ids and escalate to account team for potential credits.

sam_runtime: Repro update (10m): I reproduced inflated numeric hallucinations when the request was served by redwood/open-llama-7b-q4f@v1.0. 13B v2.4 produces correct numbers in my tests. Attaching short diff in logs.

sam_runtime: Quick snippet from my test logs:
```
Served model: redwood/open-llama-7b-q4f@v1.0
Prompt: What is the annual revenue and who is the CEO of LedgerPro?
Response: LedgerPro reported $420M ARR in 2023, CEO: Aaron West.
Logit highlights: token probs show spike for 420M vs 45M in 13B run.
```

marcus_eng: OK — that confirms fallback is the root cause. Sam, can you propose a short-term mitigation (revert routing or increase threshold) and a long-term fix (adjust quant calibration or prevent factuality-sensitive endpoints from falling back)?

sam_runtime: Short-term: revert routing_policy to capacity-first for hosted; immediate change to avoid 7B fallback. Long-term: add content-integrity-aware routing that disables fallback for queries flagged as fact-lookup (heuristic + prompt tags). Also plan a quant re-calibration run for the 7B artifact.

lia_product: I'll open a product ticket for content-integrity routing and coordinate with infra for rollout plan.

elena_cs: Customer notified — offered to pin to 13B and provided temporary credits. They're appreciative and will confirm if the issue stops after routing revert. :thumbsup:

marcus_eng: Thanks team. Please post final notes when routing change is applied and whether FinLedger sees improvement.

elena_cs: Will follow up. Closing loop after customer confirmation.
